This study examines the compressible Navier-Stokes equations, which model the transport of mass, momentum, and energy within a viscous, heat-conducting, and compressible fluid. The analysis incorporates the principle of non-negative specific entropy and the specific heat ratio $\gamma > 1$. The primary objective is to establish the existence of global-in-time weak solutions that remain uniformly bounded in entropy. The proof relies on the construction of an approximate solution via the viscous regularization method, combined with the application of the relative entropy technique and the dissipation of relative entropy.

This study evaluates various machine learning algorithms to forecast the probability of default on non-performing loans (NPLs) using data from the Kaggle NPL dataset. The analysis examines the impact of different feature engineering techniques, including the significance of individual variables and the relative importance of features. The research also investigates how varying the number of features influences predictive accuracy. Ultimately, the paper aims to identify the optimal machine learning algorithm for predicting default risk on NPLs.

We establish a connection between these polynomials and the chromatic symmetric polynomials of the order ideals within the poset, a result that recovers the Dyck path poset poset when the parameter q equals 1. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these polynomials are Schur positive and provide a combinatorial interpretation for the coefficients of elementary symmetric functions. Our proof leverages the Edelman-Garsia bijection, which establishes an isomorphism between the weak order of the poset and the weak order of the poset of standard Young tableaux. We introduce the Orientation Convolutional Network (OCN), a novel architecture designed to leverage the inherent orientation of image features for classification. The OCN employs a specialized oriented convolutional layer that learns orientation-specific filters, which are subsequently aggregated via an orientation-invariant pooling layer. This approach effectively captures both local oriented structures and global image context. Experimental results on the MNIST and FashionMNIST datasets demonstrate that the OCN achieves state-of-the-art performance with significantly fewer parameters and faster training times compared to existing methods.

We introduce a new relative trace formula applicable to a pair of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ twisted forms of $\mathrm{AL}_2$ defined over a number field. This formula establishes a correspondence linking the spectral side to automorphic representations with the arithmetic side to algebraic points on the variety of relative trace curves. This work extends the achievements of the paper by Clozel and Mok, who utilized a relative trace formula for linear intervals of $\mathrm{AL}_2$ over a number field to establish their main theorem.

This study investigates the chromatic index of the subset of nodes within a graph $G$, denoted as $\chi_{\text{sub}}(G)$, defined as the minimum number of colors required to edge-color $G$ such that every node with at least two incident edges is assigned a distinct color from its neighbors. We demonstrate that for any graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$, the inequality $\chi_{\text{sub}}(G) \leq \Delta + 1$ holds. Furthermore, we establish that $\chi_{\text{sub}}(G) = \Delta$ whenever $G$ is nearly regular, meaning the count of nodes with degree $\Delta$ is at most one greater than the count of nodes with degree $\Delta - 1$. Additionally, we prove that $\chi_{\text{sub}}(G) = \Delta$ if the count of nodes with degree $\Delta$ is at most two times the count of nodes with degree $\Delta - 1$. Finally, we show that $\chi_{\text{sub}}(G) = \Delta$ whenever the count of nodes with degree $\Delta$ is at most the count of nodes with degree $\Delta - 1$ plus the count of nodes with degree $\Delta - 2$.

This study investigates the hypercontractivity within weighted Berman spaces, a class of function spaces that encompasses both classical weighted Bergman spaces and the Fock spaces. We derive a precise characterization of the hypercontractive constant for these spaces and demonstrate that this constant can be expressed as the supremum of a specific function defined over the parameters of the weight. Furthermore, we establish a sharp version of the hypercontractive inequality for weighted Fock spaces.

The rapid spread of the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) has triggered a global pandemic, with chest computed tomography (CT) scans serving as a vital diagnostic tool for detecting the disease. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the high complexity of the task have hindered the development of effective deep learning models. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel two-stage time-distributed capsule network (TD-CN) designed to enhance detection accuracy. This approach employs a time-distributed capsule network as a feature extractor, followed by a routing capsule network for classification. Experimental results indicate that our method achieves a 99.9% accuracy rate on the COVID-19 dataset, surpassing existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study examines the use of Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) space, a region increasingly vital for satellite deployment. It outlines the physical characteristics of LEO and analyzes the orbital dynamics governing satellite trajectories. Furthermore, the paper explores the primary applications of LEO satellites, including communication, navigation, and remote sensing. It also investigates the growing challenge of space debris and proposes mitigation strategies. Finally, the work concludes with a summary of the key findings and an outlook on future research directions.

This paper introduces a novel approach for generating high-order unstructured grids on CAD models, utilizing a method that combines surface triangulation with the integer linear optimization of quad meshing. The process begins by creating a surface triangulation, where each triangle is assigned a quad patch to form a coarse quad grid. Subsequently, the geometry of these quad patches is refined to produce a high-order coarse quad grid. The primary innovation lies in the quad patch optimization, which employs an integer linear optimization framework to determine the optimal number of quads per patch and the corresponding high-order element connectivity. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through several numerical examples.

This study derives analytical formulas for the sample moments of the sample correlation coefficient, calculated across all feasible data arrangements within a specified sample space. These formulas are applicable to datasets comprising $n$ observations drawn from $p$ variables, where each observation is a vector of $p$ real numbers. The derived expressions for the first and second sample moments of the correlation coefficient are validated through numerical simulations.

We introduce a general-relativistic extension of the $S$-matrix method, which is typically used in quantum mechanics. This approach involves solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for a system's wave function, which is then transformed into the energy domain to yield the $S$-matrix. We demonstrate that this method can be applied to gravitational waves, thereby providing a novel perspective on general relativity.

This study examines the stabilization of the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations within critical Sobolev and Besov spaces. By utilizing a finite-dimensional, internally located feedback control, the authors establish uniform exponential stabilization for solutions in the $L^q$-based Sobolev space $H^{2-2/q}_q(\Omega)$ and in the $\dot{B}^{2-2/q}_q(\Omega)$-based Besov space $\dot{B}^{2-2/q}_q(\Omega)$, where $\Omega$ represents a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a smooth boundary.

This paper introduces the Lexicon of Late Imperial and Republican Chinese Texts (LitMind), a freely accessible, user-friendly dictionary designed to support scholars studying pre-Qin and Han Chinese literature. Developed by the LitMind project, this resource aims to facilitate the study of classical Chinese texts through an integrated approach combining lexicography, philology, and textual criticism. The dictionary currently features over 100,000 entries, including more than 100,000 unique glosses, compiled from various authoritative sources. It offers comprehensive definitions, etymological analyses, and contextual examples for each term. The platform also provides advanced search capabilities, allowing users to query entries, cross-references, and illustrative examples, as well as access detailed bibliographic citations for all cited examples. The dictionary is continuously updated and expanded to include new entries and examples as they become available. Explainable recommendation systems (RecSys) are increasingly vital for enhancing user experience and engagement. While methods like Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) have been widely adopted to generate explanations for black-box RecSys, they often suffer from instability and lack of consistency. This paper introduces a novel approach to crafting black-box RecSys explanations that are both stable and consistent. We demonstrate that the instability of current explanations stems from a lack of "commitment" to the underlying model. To address this, we propose a commitment-based methodology that ensures explanations remain stable and consistent across varying inputs. We also present a theoretical framework for commitment-based explanations and provide empirical evidence showing that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of stability and consistency.

This study examines the Fermi level anchoring effect in InAs quantum wells (QWs) situated near the surface of InP substrates. We demonstrate that the Fermi level is pinned to the midgap by a combination of surface states and a bulk defect, specifically the EL2 level. To mitigate this pinning, we implemented a strategy involving the introduction of a compensating donor, which successfully shifted the Fermi level toward the conduction band edge. This approach was validated through a comprehensive analysis of temperature-dependent Hall effect and capacitance-voltage data.

Resilient learning represents a significant challenge in machine learning, where the objective is to train a model using a dataset contaminated with poisoned samples. This study examines the efficacy of Regional Queries (RQ), a technique that trains on regional subsets of data rather than the full set, in mitigating poison ing. We demonstrate that RQ can effectively reduce the impact of adversaries, provided that the regional subsets are sufficiently small and numerous. Furthermore, we establish that RQ is ineffective when regional subsets are large and sparse. These findings are supported by theoretical analysis and empirical validation across various poisoning attacks.

This paper introduces a novel, efficient algorithm for computing the optimal transport plan between two discrete measures of size $n$. By leveraging the structure of triangular and diagonal matrices, the proposed method achieves precise computation in linear time, $O(n)$, while maintaining numerical stability. The approach is built upon the Quick Sinkhorn algorithm, a recent iterative technique for exact optimal transport calculations. The study provides a rigorous mathematical proof of the algorithm's convergence and demonstrates its effectiveness through experiments on synthetic data, highlighting its superior performance compared to existing methods.

This study presents the first FUV observations of the young, active M-dwarf AU Mic, utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope's Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) to capture data during both quiescent and eruptive phases. The results indicate that the star's FUV emission is dominated by its photosphere, with coronal contributions being negligible. The photospheric emission is modeled using a blackbody fit, yielding an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff} = 3300 \pm 100$ K. The coronal component is estimated to be approximately 1% of the total FUV flux, which is roughly 100 times lower than the star's X-ray flux. Consequently, the coronal FUV emission is insufficient to account for the observed exospheric mass loss in the system's known planets. The study also examines the star's eruptive behavior, noting that eruptions increase the FUV flux by a factor of 10 to 100 relative to the quiescent state. The FUV flare energy ($E_{\rm flare}$) correlates with the X-ray flare energy ($E_{\rm X}$) via a power law with an index of $\alpha = 1.5$. We investigate the impact of resistive effects on the motion of a heavy probe within a medium, modeling the substance as a collection of particles that emit radiation upon interaction with the probe. By analyzing the probe's trajectory, we demonstrate that the resulting drag force is proportional to the medium's electrical resistivity. Furthermore, we examine the implications of this finding for the energy loss mechanisms of heavy quarks in a quark-gluon plasma.

This paper introduces a statistical approach to address classification challenges arising from imbalanced datasets. The proposed method involves partitioning the data into subsets based on class labels, calculating the mean vector and covariance matrix for each subset, and then determining the probability density function for every class using these statistics. Classification is achieved by assigning a new data point to the class with the highest probability density. The study evaluates this statistical method against the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm across various scenarios, including equal and unequal sample sizes, and different data distributions. The results indicate that the proposed statistical method outperforms KNN in most tested cases.

We introduce a novel sample of 1,000 Ultra-Bright Quasar (UBQ) candidates identified through the SkyMapper Southern Survey, with redshifts exceeding 2.0 and absolute $r$-band magnitudes fainter than $-24.5$. These candidates were selected using a color-based method that effectively distinguishes quasars from stars and galaxies. Our analysis of the sample reveals that 96% are confirmed quasars, with 94% of those detections verified via spectroscopy. The remaining 4% are likely quasars that remain undetected spectroscopically due to observational limitations. We estimate the absolute $r$-band magnitude limit for our spectroscopically confirmed quasars to be $-24.5$ at 95% confidence, though this limit may extend to $-25.5$ at 90% confidence. Consequently, our spectroscopically confirmed sample represents the most luminous quasar population observed to date. We also present a new luminosity function for these Ultra-Bright Quasars, which exhibits a steep decline at the faint end and a flat profile at the bright end, with a luminosity function value of $10^{-3.5}$ at $M_r = -25.5$. Additionally, we provide a new estimate for the quasar occupation fraction at $z=2.5$, finding it to be $10^{-1.5

We introduce a novel experimental technique to detect the tunneling of electrons between a quantum dot and a superconducting lead by monitoring charge fluctuations within an adjacent, non-superconducting quantum dot. This approach enables the investigation of how superconducting proximity effects influence the charge dynamics of a nearby quantum dot. Our findings reveal that the tunneling rate between the superconducting lead and the quantum dot is significantly modulated by the charge state of the neighboring dot. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the quantum dot's charge fluctuations can be controlled by adjusting the chemical potential of the superconducting terminal.

This study establishes a contraction principle for the entropic discontinuities observed in systems of conservation laws. We demonstrate that these specific discontinuities satisfy all contraction criteria defined by the $L^1$ distance under the entropy metric, applicable to both scalar equations and systems involving multiple dimensions. Furthermore, we introduce a novel framework for constructing the entropy metric across systems of conservation laws, a method that proves effective for deriving the contraction constants associated with entropic discontinuities.

This study introduces DiffDreamer, a conditional diffusion system designed to generate consistent multi-view imagery from a single input image. By leveraging pre-trained, view-conditioned diffusion models, our approach synthesizes unseen perspectives by conditioning on specific view angles. To ensure spatial coherence across generated images, we employ a multi-stage training strategy that first establishes a base model capable of producing view-consistent outputs, followed by fine-tuning to enhance image quality. Furthermore, we develop a novel loss function to optimize the alignment between generated images and their corresponding view prompts. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques in terms of both visual quality and consistency.

This study introduces a data-driven approach to forecast, improve, and manage the evolution of networked processes, specifically utilizing the Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible (SIS) epidemic model on networks. The proposed framework employs a data-centric methodology to predict the future state of the system, enhance the quality of historical data, and determine optimal control strategies. The underlying prediction and enhancement mechanisms are grounded in a framework of nonlinear dynamical systems, which are approximated using a nonlinear autoregressive moving average (nonlinear ARMAX) model. The prediction phase leverages this model to estimate the system's future trajectory, while the enhancement phase applies it to reconstruct the system's past states from noisy observations. Furthermore, the control strategy utilizes the prediction model to identify the most effective control inputs for achieving desired outcomes. The efficacy of this approach is validated through simulations on both synthetic and real-world networks, demonstrating its robustness and potential for practical application.

This study examines the instability of a thin liquid film coating a solid cylinder, with a specific focus on the influence of slip at the interface. The analysis reveals that slip can either suppress or accelerate the Rayleigh-Plateau instability, contingent upon the slip length relative to the film thickness. The findings are validated against prior research on no-slip conditions and align with recent experimental data.

The paper presents a novel Lipschitz stability estimate for the Hunter-Saxton formula, which expresses the curvature of a surface in terms of the geodesic connection of its conformal metric. This result is a fundamental component of the proof establishing the conformal invariance of the Gauss-Bonnet theorem for conformally hyperbolic surfaces, a theorem originally conjectured by J. M. Bismuth.

This study investigates the reliability of a robotic ultrasound system for scoliosis assessment, contrasting it with conventional manual scanning. The research focuses on the spine's longitudinal axis, a critical metric for scoliosis evaluation. The robotic system employs a 2D linear array probe, a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) kinematic chain, and an integrated image processing algorithm to automatically detect the axis. The investigation involved 10 participants, with each spine region scanned three times by both a human expert and the robot. The analysis utilized the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) to assess the repeatability of measurements from both methods. The results indicate that the robotic ultrasound system achieves measurement reliability comparable to that of the manual approach.

This study introduces a non-statistical approach to determine the duration of synthesized speech by calculating the median of the acoustic energy across all frames. By eliminating the need for training, this method avoids the computational overhead and statistical complexities associated with traditional models. Consequently, it offers a highly efficient and effective solution for estimating speech lengths.

Detecting hate speech is a critical challenge for social media platforms, given the rapid growth of online content. This paper introduces a novel model designed to identify hate speech by leveraging character-level features. The proposed approach utilizes a character-based convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from input text, which are then processed by a fully connected neural network to generate classification results. The study evaluates the model's performance on the English subset of the HateXplain dataset, demonstrating that it achieves superior accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a novel feature sharing mechanism for Multi-input Multi-output (MIMO) architectures, designed to enhance the efficiency of existing MIMO frameworks. The proposed method involves partitioning the MIMO structure into multiple sub-networks, each dedicated to processing a specific subset of input channels. These sub-networks are then linked through a feature sharing module that utilizes a lightweight, learnable transformation matrix to facilitate information exchange. The approach is validated on the CIFAR-100 dataset, demonstrating significant performance gains: a 1.5% increase in top-1 accuracy and a 1.2% increase in top-5 accuracy compared to the baseline MIMO architecture.

Historical records, such as old photographs, maps, and manuscripts, are vital cultural assets that require extensive digitization efforts. These documents often feature degraded quality due to factors like poor lighting, noise, and skewed angles. To facilitate research in image restoration, this paper reviews 18 publicly available historical document datasets, categorizing them into three groups: manuscripts, maps, and photographs. We analyze each collection's characteristics, including image resolution, degradation types, and associated metadata. Furthermore, we evaluate the utility of these datasets for restoration tasks, including denoising, enhancement, and deskewing.

This study introduces a control method for an industrial robot joint that utilizes auxiliary encoders to enhance position tracking performance. The proposed system employs a feedback linearization controller, which is augmented by a feedforward term derived from a model of the robot dynamics. This dynamic model is estimated using data from the auxiliary encoders. The resulting controller ensures the position tracking error converges to zero asymptotically. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms standard industrial controllers in terms of position tracking accuracy.

This study introduces a multidimensional framework designed to analyze multiple time-to-occurrence data, specifically targeting recurrent events within a single subject. The proposed model integrates multiple states, allowing for the simultaneous estimation of the time until a state transition and the subsequent duration within that state. This approach is particularly valuable for healthcare research, as it captures the complex, heterogeneous trajectories of patients with chronic conditions. The paper details the model's formulation, estimation procedures, and evaluation through a simulation study. Furthermore, the method is applied to real-world data concerning patients with myocardial infarction, demonstrating its utility in mapping diverse health pathways.

This study introduces a multi-site quadrature approach designed to solve the molecular continuum equation, which models the transport of vibrationally excited molecules. The method employs a system of coupled, time-dependent Boltzmann equations, each corresponding to a specific vibrational state. By utilizing a quadrature-based representation of the distribution function, the method converts the complex integro-differential equation into a set of simpler partial differential equations. The system is solved using a hybrid scheme combining finite differences in time with finite volumes in space. The study evaluates the method's performance through a benchmark test case and compares its results against a standard Monte Carlo simulation.

The metric dimension of a graph represents the smallest possible size of a vertex subset such that every other vertex possesses a distinct distance vector relative to this set. This study investigates the complexity of determining metric dimension when parameterized by graph structures that are closely linked to the graph's feedback vertex number. Specifically, we demonstrate that metric dimension is W[1]-hard when parameterized by the graph's vertex cover size, and it remains W[1]-hard even under the restriction to chordal graphs when parameterized by tree-depth. Furthermore, we establish that the problem is W[1]-hard for general graphs parameterized by the size of a specific vertex set where every vertex outside this set has exactly two neighbors within it. In contrast, we prove that an algorithm exists which computes metric dimension in f(k)·n time for any function f, using k as the parameter for the graph's maximum degree and n as the number of vertices.

This paper introduces a novel framework for directed topology, termed the "authority framework," which is built upon the concept of "authority maps." We establish the authority maps as a subcategory of the category of directed continuous functions, demonstrating that it forms a monoidal category under composition and tensor product. Furthermore, we define "directed homomorphisms" as the directed analog of standard function homomorphisms and prove that the category of such homomorphisms is equivalent to the category of directed sets and directed continuous functions. Finally, we explore the authority maps in relation to the subcategory of directed topological spaces and their corresponding homomorphisms.

This study examines simulated climate data from the last 200,000 years, revealing that Earth's temperature history is characterized by a long-term warming trend punctuated by abrupt cooling episodes. These sudden drops, which occurred roughly every 100,000 years, coincide with the termination of glacial periods. The research demonstrates that the timing and magnitude of these thermal shifts are governed by the planet's orbital mechanics, specifically the precession of the equinoxes. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that the climate system exhibits a critical threshold; once the rate of long-term warming surpasses a specific point, the system undergoes a rapid transition to a new stable state, resulting in a significant drop in temperature.

We introduce a unified twistor framework for self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) and its higher-spin extension, both of which are formulated as holomorphic bundles over a modified, extended version of standard twistor space. In this setup, the higher-spin extension corresponds to a line bundle, whereas SDYM is represented by a vector bundle. The line bundle's linear transition functions are derived from a Lie algebra valued function, while the vector bundle's transition functions are determined by a Lie group valued function. The resulting higher-spin extension of SDYM is shown to be equivalent to a system of Lie algebra valued twististor equations.

Medical image classification is a critical area of research, yet the scarcity of labeled data and the high cost of expert annotation often result in noisy labels, which severely degrade classifier performance. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian statistics-driven mechanism for renovating label renovation in medical images. This approach utilizes a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to create realistic synthetic data, which then informs a Bayesian classifier to estimate the probability of label correctness. By employing a Monte Carlo dropout technique, the model captures posterior uncertainty, enabling the identification and correction of label errors. Experimental results on two prominent medical image datasets demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper establishes an upper limit on the norm of an interpolation operator within a quasi-interpolation framework. It also derives a lower limit on the norm of an inverse interpolation operator, applicable to various scenarios.

We introduce a novel method to determine the transition probabilities of a random walk on a graph by utilizing its distinctive polynomial. This approach establishes a correspondence between a graph and its related random walk, enabling the determination of the random walk's transition probability matrix solely from graph-theoretic data.

This paper introduces a timed definition framework within the HOL logic, which extends standard definitions by incorporating a timing constraint on the function's execution. We present a method for verifying these constraints and demonstrate the utility of this extension in the context of real-time system development.

This study introduces a data-driven methodology designed to refine the instantaneous prediction of wall turbulence in the context of the Lagrangian coherent structure (LCS) model. The approach involves training a deep neural network (DNN) to forecast the temporal evolution of the unstable manifold associated with hyperbolic fixed points, which are identified as the unstable LCS. The DNN is trained on a dataset generated by the particle tracking method, which simulates the forward time integration of the unstable manifold. The resulting coherent structure-based model, enhanced by this data-informed DNN, is evaluated against direct numerical simulation (DNS) data for wall turbulence. The findings indicate that the improved model significantly outperforms the standard LCS model, achieving a reduction in prediction error by a factor of 10 to 100.

We investigate a newly proposed Born-Infeld extension of the Skyrme model, which incorporates a Skyrme-type stabilizing potential. This model supports both finite-energy soliton solutions and self-dual configurations. The finite-energy sector encompasses the standard Skyrmion, a magnetic monopole, and a previously unidentified soliton. Furthermore, we demonstrate that magnetic monopole and vortex solutions satisfy a first-order self-duality equation. Finally, we analyze the model's behavior in the limit where the Skyrme term is removed.

We introduce a theoretical model of a two-dimensional lattice featuring Weyl nodes that lack time-reversal symmetry, situated within the Hofstadter regime. By examining the energy spectrum, we demonstrate that the nodes manifest as pairs of opposite chirality, separated by a magnetic flux of $eB = 2\pi p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime integers. Furthermore, we calculate the topological invariants of the system and derive the corresponding low-energy effective Hamiltonian.

This study introduces a hybrid dielectric-plasmonic nanoantenna designed to generate highly efficient, directional, and single-color single-photon sources. The proposed structure integrates a plasmonic bowtie antenna with a dielectric nanoparticle, which together support a highly confined hybrid mode. This configuration supports a quantum dot (QD) placed within the field of view, resulting in a significant enhancement of the QD's radiative decay rate. The resulting photon source exhibits superior performance in terms of brightness, directionality, and spectral purity. The work provides a promising route toward advanced quantum photonic applications.

This study introduces a new framework for understanding the nonlinear screening of contact forces within granular assemblies. The proposed theory posits that contact force screening is governed by the same mechanisms driving screening in charged particles, albeit with distinct force laws. Specifically, the theory predicts that the average contact force scales with the number of contacts ($N$) according to a power law, $F \propto N^{-\alpha}$, where the exponent $\alpha$ varies with the applied stress. Experimental results confirm this prediction, revealing that the exponent $\alpha$ increases as applied stress rises. Furthermore, the theory successfully accounts for the observed dependence of the average coordination number on applied stress.

This study investigates the electronic properties of silicene grown on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) with adsorbed manganese atoms. We examine various configurations, including single Mn atoms, small clusters, and large clusters, to determine their impact on the substrate's electronic structure. Our findings reveal that while single Mn atoms and small clusters induce localized magnetic moments, large clusters fail to do so. Furthermore, the presence of Mn atoms generates a band gap in the hBN-supported system, transforming it from a semimetal into a semiconductor.

Sgr A East is a supernova remnant situated near the Galactic Center, with its origin traced to a stellar explosion that occurred roughly 10,000 years ago. This study investigates the location of the progenitor star by analyzing the spatial distribution of the remnant's X-ray emission. We find that the X-ray emitting region is elongated along the Galactic plane, with its major axis aligned approximately 10° from the Galactic center. This alignment suggests the progenitor star was located within the Galactic plane, approximately 10° away from the Galactic center. This finding contradicts the prevailing hypothesis that the progenitor was a massive star in the Galactic bulge, which would have resulted in a remnant aligned with the Galactic center. This study evaluates various oversampling strategies for multi-class text categorization, specifically analyzing the impact of oversampling on classification accuracy and the resulting class distributions. We examine three distinct oversampling methods: (1) the standard approach utilizing the SMOTE algorithm, (2) a modified SMOTE that incorporates text-specific features, and (3) a technique based on generating synthetic samples from a trained generative model. Experiments were conducted across three datasets with differing characteristics, employing both a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and a Naive Bayes classifier. Our findings indicate that while oversampling can enhance classification accuracy, it may also skew class distributions; furthermore, the study demonstrates that the SMOTE algorithm is not always the optimal choice for text categorization tasks.

This study investigates the relationship between COVID-19 coverage in regional U.S. news and the pandemic's impact on audiences, specifically examining how coverage levels correlate with case counts, death tolls, and viewership. Utilizing data from 2020, the research analyzed 1,000 news stories across 100 markets alongside viewership metrics. The findings indicate that news coverage is not merely a reaction to the crisis but also influences public response. Specifically, higher coverage correlates with increased case numbers and deaths, while simultaneously reducing viewership. The study further identifies that the timing of coverage matters; early reporting is linked to higher subsequent case numbers, whereas later coverage is associated with higher death tolls. Additionally, the volume of coverage is a significant factor, with more stories correlating to higher death rates. The research also highlights disparities across regions, noting that the Northeast and Midwest experienced higher coverage and worse outcomes compared to the South and West. Finally, the study underscores the role of media literacy, suggesting that individuals with greater awareness of the risks are more likely to engage with news coverage.

The Rapid Multipole Method (RMM) is a technique designed to accelerate the computation of multipole interactions, which are otherwise slow using direct methods. In this study, we present an RMM implementation that preserves angular momentum, a feature that enhances the accuracy of calculations involving angular-dependent potentials. Additionally, we demonstrate that this conservation property can be extended to the entire RMM procedure, including the translation step.

The polarization transfer in the elastic $e p \to e p$ reaction is examined within the framework of the quark parton model. The analysis indicates that polarization transfer is governed by the same dynamics as unpolarized elastic scattering, specifically the ratio of the structure functions $G_{\mathrm{T}}/G_{\mathrm{L}}$. Consequently, the predicted polarization transfer aligns with experimental data.

We introduce a novel learning framework where a parametric expert provides labels for a dataset; this expert's parameters are subsequently updated using the labeled data. This cycle repeats iteratively, with the expert generating labels for an expanded dataset in each round. We demonstrate that this approach can significantly boost data utility, enabling the model to achieve performance comparable to that of a model trained on vast amounts of data from the outset. We establish theoretical guarantees for this method, including convergence rates and error bounds, and validate our findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world data.

This study reports on the search for double Higgs boson production alongside a vector boson ($V = \gamma$, $Z$, or $W$) in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV using ATLAS detector data from the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis targets final states comprising two bosons decaying into two photons, two $Z$ bosons, or a $W$ and a $Z$ boson, with the vector boson manifesting as either a single lepton or a pair of leptons. The search employs a matrix-element-based technique to distinguish signal from background, utilizing a template-fitting approach to extract the signal yield. No significant excess beyond the predicted background is observed. Consequently, 95% confidence level upper limits on the cross-section times branching ratio for $pp \to HHV$ are established, with the most stringent limits applying to the $pp \to \gamma ZZ$ channel.

We introduce a novel concept for an optical spin laser utilizing an alkali metal vapor, driven by a radio-frequency field to induce transitions between hyperfine ground states. This system is capable of generating laser light at a frequency that is highly sensitive to the applied radio-frequency field, thereby enabling the detection of minute variations in that field.

Estimating the genus of a graph is a notoriously difficult challenge, with the best existing approximation algorithms yielding results no better than a factor of $O(\sqrt{n})$. This paper introduces a novel, efficient algorithm capable of approximating the genus of dense graphs within a factor of $O(n)$, representing a significant improvement over previous bounds for dense graphs. The proposed method relies on a new algorithm that computes the genus of a graph's bridgeless planarization in polynomial time. Additionally, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of the genus of graphs featuring a small treewidth.

This study introduces a Newton-based approach for distributed convex optimization across a network of agents. The method operates by having agents collaboratively estimate a global Newton direction for the objective function, which is then utilized to locally update their variables. The framework is designed to handle general network structures and incorporates constraints on both the global objective and individual agent feasible sets. The analysis demonstrates that, under mild assumptions, the method converges to the optimal solution within a finite number of iterations. Furthermore, the convergence rate is proven to be independent of the network's size. Numerical experiments validate these theoretical findings.

This study presents an end-to-end neural network approach for identifying Bengali and Hindi hate-speech. The work includes a detailed examination of the newly developed Bengali and Hindi Hate-Speech Datasets, which feature annotated examples of hate-speech, non-hate-speech, and offensive-but-non-hate-speech. The research evaluates various neural network architectures, including LSTM, Bi-LSTM, CNN, and a hybrid CNN-LSTM model, while also exploring transfer learning strategies. The findings indicate that transfer learning yields superior results compared to training from scratch, with the hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture achieving the highest accuracy.

Gas Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are widely employed in dark matter detection to identify nuclear recoils resulting from interactions with Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). This study introduces a novel approach for gas TPCs that enables the direct measurement of the recoil nucleus's kinetic energy and scattering angle. By utilizing a high-resolution readout system, researchers can determine the precise positions of both the initial ionization cloud and the recoil nucleus, allowing for the calculation of the scattering angle. Simultaneously, the recoil energy is derived from the total ionization charge, which is corrected for the effects of recombination. The paper outlines the methodology for these measurements and presents a simulation of the resulting distributions for recoil energy and scattering angle.

This study introduces a novel framework for assessing automated driving systems by integrating expert supervision. We present a contextual smart choice model that enables experts to monitor machine outputs, intervening only when necessary to ensure safety. This approach offers a fairer evaluation of commercial vehicles by accounting for the specific contexts in which human drivers make smart choices to correct machine errors. We validate this framework through a comprehensive analysis of over 100,000 miles of real-world data from a leading commercial vehicle manufacturer, demonstrating that our method yields significantly more consistent and reliable results than current evaluation techniques.

This document serves as a formal report detailing the Out-of-Context (OOC) challenge, a collaborative effort involving the OOC Organizing Committee and the OOC Challenge Organizing Committee. The report outlines the motivation behind the OOC initiative, its specific objectives, and the associated evaluation metrics. Furthermore, it describes the dataset employed, the baseline models utilized, and the submission protocols. The report concludes with a summary of the challenge outcomes, including the performance of participating systems and the results of an ablation study.

We examine the geodesic paths within Gaussian stochastic field manifolds, a framework that models the probability distribution of a system's state space. In this context, the mean-field dynamics are represented by the average geodesic path, while the system's state-space uncertainty is captured by the dispersion of these paths. The study focuses on a specific class of Gaussian stochastic field manifolds, where the mean-field dynamics are governed by a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) and the dispersion dynamics are described by a second-order PDE. Furthermore, the paper establishes a connection between geodesic paths and the mean-field dynamics of the system.

This work examines the distribution of long counts in random binary sequences, specifically focusing on cases where the sequence repeats every $p$ symbols. We analyze how these counts distribute as the sequence length approaches infinity, and we determine the corresponding mean and variance for finite-length sequences. Furthermore, we explore the application of these findings to the "Periodically" game film.

This paper establishes boundedness for the largest and smallest relative factors of L-functions associated with modular forms, specifically within the context of a fixed modularity type. The proof leverages the method of moments, utilizing the recent breakthrough by Blomer, Ruzsa, and Soundararajan on the boundedness of these L-factors. Furthermore, the study derives significant consequences for the boundedness of the largest and smallest relative Galois conjugates of L-factors, as well as the boundedness of the largest and smallest relative roots of these L-factors.

We investigate the transport properties of armchair graphene nanostructures, specifically focusing on the tunability of spin-dependent phenomena. By applying a perpendicular magnetic field, we demonstrate that the system can be switched between a non-magnetic regime and a spin-polarized regime. This transition is governed by the interplay between the Zeeman energy and the spin-orbit coupling. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of an in-plane electric field on the system's electronic structure and conductance characteristics.

This paper establishes two Korovkin-type theorems for weakly nonlinear and monotonic positive linear operators acting on the space $C[a,b]$. Additionally, we demonstrate that our findings encompass several established results within the field.

A graph $G$ is defined as $k$-autonomous if every $k$-coloring of its edges permits a perfect matching within each color class. This paper establishes that every $k$-autonomous graph with an even number of vertices possesses a Hamiltonian cycle. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any even order, a $k$-autonomous graph is pancyclic unless it is a complete bipartite graph. These findings are derived from a broader theorem concerning the Hamiltonian cycles of $k$-autonomous graphs with an odd number of vertices, which are shown to be Hamiltonian provided they are not isomorphic to a specific graph $H_k$.

We present an analysis of directed flow ($v_1$) for charged particles and identified hadrons in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\textrm{NN}}}$ = 200 GeV, alongside measurements from $^{196}$Au+Au and $^{208}$Pb+$^{208}$Pb systems. The study examines the dependence of $v_1$ on transverse momentum ($p_{\textrm{T}}$) across rapidity ($y$) ranges of $|y| < 0.5$ and $|y| < 1.0$. Results indicate that $v_1$ increases with $p_{\textrm{T}}$ for both rapidity intervals, with a notably stronger rise observed in the $|y| < 0.5$ region. Additionally, $v_1$ is found to be larger in Au+Au collisions than in $^{196}$Au+Au collisions, while the $^{196}$Au+Au data aligns with predictions from a transport model. In contrast, $v_1$ measurements for Pb+Pb collisions are consistent with those from Au+Au.

This study introduces a novel Adaptive Spectral Koopman (ASK) framework designed to estimate the Koopman operator for nonlinear dynamical systems. The approach utilizes a sparse grid strategy to efficiently approximate the infinite-dimensional observables, with adaptive refinement applied to the domain based on local error metrics. The method's efficacy is validated through two case studies: a linear system with time delays and a nonlinear chaotic system.

This study introduces a complex complex scaling method designed to determine the ionization energies of one-electron atoms and many-electron systems, such as multi-electron atoms and molecules, subjected to intense direct current (DC) fields. The approach is termed "outward complex scaling" because it involves shifting the integration boundary outward along the real axis during the solution of the Schr\"odinger equation. This technique is particularly advantageous for strong DC fields, where the ionization potential is significantly lowered, causing the bound-state wave function to extend over a vast spatial region. By employing outward complex scaling, the integration domain can be minimized, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. The method's accuracy is validated through calculations of ionization energies for hydrogen, hydrogen-like ions, helium, and the hydrogen molecule across various field strengths.

We demonstrate that the Sinkhorn algorithm converges to a solution for the Schr\"odinger problem, even in cases where a solution theoretically does not exist. This result is established by reformulating the problem as a constrained optimization task and applying the primal-dual hybrid gradient method. Furthermore, we provide an analysis of the convergence rate and present numerical experiments that illustrate the algorithm's efficacy in scenarios lacking a solution.

The study presents a measurement of the top-quark pair production cross-section using data from proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV, recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC during 2012. The analysis leverages the decay channel where top quarks decay into a bottom quark and a $W$ boson, with the $W$ subsequently breaking down into either an electron or a muon paired with a neutrino. The reconstructed top-quark mass spectrum is utilized to determine the cross-section, which is calculated to be $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} = 10.1 \pm 0.2 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.4 \text{(sys)} \pm 0.2 \text{(lumi)} \text{ nb}$. This result aligns with Standard Model predictions and is consistent with measurements from other experiments.

We investigate the localization characteristics of a system composed of two one-dimensional disordered chains connected by central links. Our findings indicate that while the bulk states of the chains remain localized, the linking mechanism induces delocalized states within the system. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the density of these states exhibits a pronounced dependence on the coupling strength.

This study introduces a new class of analytic functions, denoted as $I_{\alpha,\beta}(\mu,\nu)$, which extends the Janowski class $I(\mu,\nu)$ by utilizing generalized Bessel functions. We establish several fundamental properties of this new class, including closure under convolution, subordination, and the operation of convolution with convex functions. Furthermore, we derive specific results concerning the radius of Janowski convexity for various well-known functions.

The pandemic has significantly altered human social patterns, yet the specific impacts on the spatial distribution of these interactions remain unclear. This study examines the behavioral modifications of urban activities across 292 Chinese cities from 2019 to 2020, utilizing mobile positioning data. We observe that the pandemic intensified the pre-existing spatial heterogeneity of urban interactions, with the degree of shift correlating to each city's baseline activity levels. Furthermore, the pandemic's impact varied across different activity types, with some shifting more drastically than others. These findings offer critical insights into the pandemic's consequences on urban social dynamics and provide a foundation for future research and policy-making.

This study evaluates the performance of two field-split nonlinear preconditioners applied to a multiphase flow model within heterogeneous porous media. The proposed method decomposes the nonlinear system into separate equations for each phase, which are solved independently using standard preconditioners before merging the results. The research demonstrates that this preconditioning strategy significantly accelerates convergence for both the Full Displacement Model (FDM) and the Popular Multiphase Flow Model (PMFM). Furthermore, the study analyzes the impact of varying the number of phases and the degree of heterogeneity on FDM and PMFM convergence rates. The findings indicate that the field-split preconditioner is particularly effective for systems with a high degree of heterogeneity and a large number of phases.

We demonstrate that the Liouville CFT partition function, when restricted to the JT gravity bound, aligns with the partition function of the matrix model proposed by Mariño and Zaffaroni. This correspondence is established by mapping the matrix model's eigenvalue distribution to the CFT's partition function through a specific transformation. Furthermore, we show that the matrix model's free energy can be derived from the CFT's free energy by applying a differential operator.

This study examines the Alcubierre spacetime within a perfect fluid framework, specifically investigating the conditions required for a solution to exist when the cosmological constant is non-zero. We demonstrate that while the Alcubierre warp drive cannot be realized as a vacuum spacetime with a non-vanishing cosmological constant, it can emerge as a valid solution within a perfect fluid model. Furthermore, we establish that the Alcubierre warp drive is attainable as a solution to the Einstein field equations for an ideal fluid, provided the cosmological constant is zero.

The GUIDES initiative, a project funded by the European Commission, aims to create a unified, interoperable, and sustainable framework for processing geospatial urban data. Its primary objective is to facilitate the development of new geospatial services and applications by integrating diverse data sources, including Open Data from the European Commission, INSPIRE, and OpenStreetMap. To achieve this, GUIDES employs a data engineering approach that utilizes open-source tools and standardized data models to build a modular, scalable, and extensible architecture. This framework is designed to support various use cases, such as urban planning, traffic management, and emergency response.

We introduce a novel diagnostic method for characterizing the heating dynamics of trapped ions, leveraging spin-dependent fluorescence to measure spin dephasing. This dephasing rate serves as a direct indicator of the thermal energy within the vibrational modes of the ion crystal. By employing this technique, we have measured the heating rates of a two-dimensional ion crystal, achieving a sensitivity of 0.01 K per second. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the dephasing rate can reveal the distribution of vibrational excitation levels among the ions, offering insights into the specific mechanisms driving the heating process.

This study introduces a comprehensive quantum mechanical approach to calculating the electromagnetic and chemical influences on Tip-Enhanced Raman Scattering (TERS). The methodology employs a TERS model grounded in the scattering Green's function formalism, utilizing a quantum mechanical description of the scattering system. The chemical influence is modeled by modifying the electronic structure of the substrate through the inclusion of a coupling term in the electronic Hamiltonian, which accounts for the interaction between the tip and the substrate. The results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately reproduces experimental data and provides valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms of TERS.

We report on observations conducted with the Sardinia Radio Telescope (SRT) at 1.4 GHz, targeting the nearby galaxies NGC 4038/9 (the Antennae), NGC 4449, and NGC 4490. These galaxies were selected for their high star formation rates and the presence of unusual star-forming regions, such as HII regions, super star clusters, and starburst knots. The study aimed to determine if the emission from these regions could be detected at this frequency and to assess the feasibility of using the SRT for similar observations. The results indicate that the SRT can successfully detect the emission from these star-forming areas, with measured flux densities ranging from 0.01 to 0.03 mJy.

The entropy alteration accompanying the entropy-driven phase transition in ammonium sulfate, $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, is examined using inelastic neutron scattering. This study reveals that the phase transition is triggered by a softening of the translational mode associated with ammonium ion rotation. Furthermore, the observed entropy change is primarily attributed to the rotational degrees of freedom of the ammonium ion, with minor contributions from lattice vibrations. These findings are consistent with prior calorimetric data and offer a comprehensive understanding of the phase transition mechanism in ammonium sulfate.

Reinforcement learning (RL) models are widely used to explain how the brain learns from experience. These models typically predict that the midbrain encodes reward prediction errors (RPEs), which are calculated as the difference between expected and actual outcomes. However, this study demonstrates that the midbrain's RPE signal is not merely a byproduct of learning but is also shaped by the specific RL strategy employed. We identified that the midbrain encodes RPEs generated by both standard and "suboptimal" (characteristic) strategies, with the latter reflecting the agent's unique behavioral traits. Furthermore, the midbrain selectively represents RPEs derived from actions that are most likely to be chosen by the agent. These findings indicate that the midbrain's RPE signal is constrained by the agent's behavioral tendencies, suggesting that the brain may utilize this signal to anticipate future actions.

This study explores quantum entanglement and contextuality within $E_8$ lattice systems, focusing on their complexified forms. We establish that the complexification of the $E_8$ lattice is isomorphic to the complexification of the Leech lattice modulo 24, demonstrating that both share identical complex structures. Furthermore, we show that the complex $E_8$ lattice decomposes into the direct sum of the complex $D_8$ lattice and an 8-dimensional complex hyperbolic space. These findings enable the construction of quantum entanglement and contextuality states using the complex $E_8$ lattice. Specifically, we identify two distinct classes of such states: one derived from the complex $D_8$ lattice and another from the complex hyperb space component. We also examine the properties of these states, including their entanglement entropy and contextuality measures. Finally, we discuss the physical implications of these results for quantum information theory and quantum field theory.

Estimating distance metrics are essential for efficiently querying large collections of time series data. This paper introduces strict theoretical limits for the worst-case performance of any estimation function applied to time series, specifically under the Fréchet distance. We demonstrate that the Fréchet distance is inherently difficult to approximate, establishing a lower bound on estimation error that escalates linearly with the length of the time series. Furthermore, we prove that the close neighbor problem under the Fréchet distance suffers from an estimation error bound that increases quadratically with the time series length. These findings indicate that estimation-based approaches are likely unsuitable for computing the Fréchet distance on time series.

Measurement error reduction (MER) is a critical component of data processing, particularly for high-precision applications like quantum metrology. This study introduces an iterative Bayesian framework designed to enhance MER performance by leveraging the redundancy inherent in repeated measurements. The proposed method, termed Iterative Bayesian Unraveling (IBU), operates by iteratively refining the posterior distribution of a parameter using data from a single measurement, thereby progressively narrowing the parameter's uncertainty. Theoretically, IBU is proven to converge to the true parameter value under specific conditions. Furthermore, the approach is demonstrated to be highly effective in the context of expandable measurements, where additional data can be acquired post-experiment to further decrease error. Numerical simulations confirm that IBU significantly outperforms standard Bayesian MER techniques, achieving superior accuracy with a notably reduced number of iterations.

The robotics sector is characterized by a fragmented landscape of diverse, often incompatible standards, which hinders the widespread adoption of robotic systems. This paper introduces Shared Autonomy as a viable strategy to facilitate the integration of these varied standards. By enabling robots to communicate and exchange information with one another, this approach allows for the creation of a cohesive robotic ecosystem. We illustrate the effectiveness of this concept through a case study involving a mobile robot tasked with delivering items to a stationary robot. The results demonstrate that the robots can successfully share information regarding their operational standards, thereby enabling them to collaborate effectively.

This paper introduces HiTMap, a hierarchical topological map representation designed for navigation in unknown environments. The proposed method utilizes a hierarchical structure to enhance both the scalability and robustness of the system. Specifically, it employs a coarse-level representation for high-level navigation and a fine-level representation for detailed local exploration. The system's efficacy is validated through extensive experiments conducted in diverse, large-scale, and complex real-world environments.

Multi-energy X-ray computed tomography (MXCT) is a rapidly developing imaging technique that offers superior material characterization and quantification compared to conventional single-energy CT. This paper introduces a novel non-convex variational framework designed to simultaneously reconstruct images from polyenergetic CT data, suppress sensor noise, and decompose materials. The proposed approach employs a unified optimization model that integrates a non-convex regularizer for enhanced image quality with a data fidelity term to ensure accurate reconstruction. To solve this model, we developed an iterative algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The efficacy of this method is validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to deliver high-quality reconstructions and effective material decomposition.

This study examines the influence of electron spill-over and nonlocal effects on gap-plasmons in the limit of shrinking gaps, revealing that these effects can induce a transition from surface plasmon-polariton (SPP) modes to gap-plasmon (GP) modes. We demonstrate that the mode profile of an SPP is defined by the electromagnetic field distribution, whereas a GP mode is governed by the electron density profile. Furthermore, we show that the nonlocal effect can be modeled as an effective electron mass, which is determined by the specific mode profile. Consequently, the nonlocal effect can be analyzed using the effective mass approximation.

This study introduces a novel interactive framework for exploring multivariate time series, leveraging the principles of screen sharing and interactivity. By utilizing a single display, this approach allows users to simultaneously view multiple longitudinal datasets and engage with them through direct manipulation. The framework supports various interaction techniques, including dragging, dragging, and querying, which can be applied to both individual data points and entire sequences. The authors present a set of design guidelines for constructing such interactive systems and illustrate their application through a case study involving a mobile health application.

Similarity measurement is vital for clinical decision support systems, yet existing methods often rely on simplistic, domain-agnostic strategies that fail to capture the complexity of medical data. To address this, we introduce a novel framework leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to model digital health records as interconnected graphs. This approach offers two distinct similarity metrics: one based on node-level representations and another on graph-level representations. The node-level metric evaluates similarity by comparing embeddings of specific health record elements, whereas the graph-level metric assesses overall record similarity by comparing the embeddings of the records' aggregate graphs. The node-level similarity is derived from the structural features of individual nodes, while the graph-level similarity utilizes the GNN to generate embeddings for the entire record structure. We validated this framework using a dataset of 1,000 electronic health records from the MIMIC-III database, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing nuanced similarities within complex medical data.

The investigation utilizes a comprehensive model that integrates the Poisson equation with the equation of state for the solvent, alongside the Boltzmann distribution for counterions and co-ions. This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically generate software specifications by processing unstructured texts. The method leverages the semantic connections between domain concepts and software engineering principles found within texts to pinpoint specific elements in the input. It employs a combination of rule-based and neural network models to identify these features, subsequently using them to construct the corresponding software specifications. The study evaluates the performance of these models across three distinct tasks: identifying domain concepts, detecting software engineering principles, and pinpointing the relationships between them.

This study addresses the challenge of minimizing total energy usage in a multi-source, multi-relay, multi-destination network by optimizing the assignment of relays and the distribution of transmission power. To achieve this, we introduce an energy-efficient collaborative network coding (ECNC) protocol. Within this framework, relays cooperatively encode data from various sources to generate a unified encoded packet, which is then forwarded to all destinations. The proposed solution employs a joint optimization approach for relay selection and power allocation, utilizing a convex optimization method to derive the optimal configuration. Simulation results demonstrate that the ECNC protocol outperforms both traditional multi-hop and multi-cast protocols in terms of energy efficiency.

This study employs a relativistic adaptation of the Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) theory to analyze the electronic properties of individual magnetic adatoms and dimers situated on Nb(110). The analysis utilizes a tight-binding model incorporating both $d$ and $f$ orbitals, with parameters derived from density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The resulting electronic spectra exhibit significant dependence on the magnetic moment, the number of conduction electrons, and the specific orbital contributions. Furthermore, the study investigates the impact of spin-orbit coupling on the spin splitting of the YSR spectrum, as well as the anisotropy of the Kondo resonance.

This study reports an initial investigation into the rare decay $K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}$ using the decay-in-flight technique. The analysis utilizes a dataset of $1.05 \times 10^{12}$ collected kaons, with a focus on events where the kaon decays into a pion and an invisible system. The results indicate an upper limit on the branching fraction of $< 1.1 \times 10^{-10}$ at 90% confidence level, which is 1.5 times more stringent than the previous best limit.

This study introduces a neural network-based filter designed to reduce bias in the widely used distribution-to-distribution scan matching algorithm. The filter operates by learning a mapping from the input point clouds to the resulting scan matching error, thereby enabling the prediction of the optimal rotation angle that corrects this error. The authors demonstrate that this filter significantly enhances the accuracy of scan matching, particularly in scenarios involving pre-existing bias.

The method relies on a specialized loss function designed to optimize the output of a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) for edge detection. The loss function is based on the assumption that edges in satellite images are sparse and can be represented as a set of points. The method is evaluated on a publicly available dataset of satellite images and compared to the results of other state-of-the-art deep learning-based edge detection methods. Non-linear X-ray absorption edge spectra, observed in high-fluence experiments, are analyzed through a rate framework that models the kinetics of excited electron populations. This approach offers a generalized perspective on non-linear absorption, applicable to any system where non-linearities stem from the occupation of excited electronic states. The study derives rate equations for both monochromatic and polychromatic excitation scenarios, providing a model for the time evolution of the population and the resulting non-linear absorption coefficient. Furthermore, the model is validated against experimental data from non-linear X-ray absorption edge spectra of copper, demonstrating its utility in describing non-linear absorption mechanisms driven by excited electronic populations.

This study introduces a novel approach to enhance modulation categorization robustness against adversarial attacks. By leveraging the generative capabilities of the proposed blend GAN, we generate adversarial examples across diverse attack methods to create a comprehensive training set. This strategy enables the modulation categorization model to learn from a broader spectrum of adversarial assaults, thereby significantly improving its resilience. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques, with accuracy gains of up to 10.1% against Fast-Fooling attacks and 10.3% against FGSM attacks.

Segmentation of brain lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS) is a critical clinical task, yet it remains difficult due to the disease's heterogeneity and the scarcity of annotated data. This study investigates the effectiveness of continuously updating segmentation models with new data from different clinics, comparing this continual learning strategy against retraining models from scratch. Using data from three clinics, we evaluate performance across various scenarios, including testing on data from unseen clinics and training on data from only a single clinic. Our findings indicate that continual learning yields superior results compared to retraining from scratch in nearly all cases. Additionally, we demonstrate that models trained continuously on data from a single clinic can achieve performance comparable to those trained on data from all three clinics combined.

We introduce a novel dual comparison method for evaluating the performance of primal and dual solutions within linear programming. This approach establishes a comparison framework that is at least as robust as the traditional duality gap yet offers greater computational efficiency. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this comparison metric can be seamlessly integrated into various primal-dual interior-point methods, resulting in algorithms capable of producing high-quality approximate solutions for the primal and dual problems simultaneously.

This study introduces a framework for machine intelligence designed to detect modeling errors in dynamical systems. It outlines a multi-level architecture where a primary "supervisor" oversees a hierarchy of specialized "critics." These critics employ various machine learning techniques to pinpoint specific discrepancies between a system's actual behavior and its current model. The authors demonstrate this approach using a case study involving a dynamical system with unknown parameters, successfully identifying mismatches between the model and reality.

We present a new simulation framework designed to investigate dark energy models based on Primordial Black Holes (PBHs). This framework utilizes the PopSyCLE code, a flexible platform capable of modeling the evolution of astrophysical populations from their origins to the present day. Our simulation tracks PBH formation, accretion, and mergers across cosmic history, ultimately calculating the PBH mass function and energy density at the current epoch. We demonstrate that the framework can reproduce results from previous studies, specifically regarding the accretion of baryonic matter and PBH merger rates. Furthermore, we explore the impact of varying formation mechanisms on the PBH mass function and energy density, ultimately deriving constraints on the PBH fraction of dark energy.

Parameter-efficient tuning has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to full fine-tuning for adapting pre-trained models to new tasks. This study introduces a novel approach, Unique Token Adaptation (UTA), which leverages the distinctiveness of specific tokens to enhance parameter efficiency. By fine-tuning only the embeddings of these unique tokens alongside a small set of query parameters, UTA achieves performance comparable to full fine-tuning while drastically reducing the number of trainable parameters. Empirical evaluations across diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that UTA outperforms existing parameter-efficient methods, offering a highly efficient solution for model adaptation.

We introduce two distinct ranking systems: the **contextual preference of sets**, which orders subsets based on the preference for adding their respective elements, and the **non-contextual preference of sets**, which ranks individual elements independently of context. We demonstrate that while the non-contextual approach is more straightforward, the contextual preference offers superior flexibility and greater freedom in modeling.
